chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
About a house whose roof is urinated upon and where ghusl from janābah is performed, then rain falls upon it: may water be taken from it and used for wudu for salat?
So he said: “If it flows, there is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the house or structure under discussion
key_terms.مَائِهِ: its water, meaning the water coming from that place
key_terms.يُبَالُ: urine is discharged; indicating possible najasah

ai.seo_question: Can rainwater flowing from a roof exposed to urine or ghusl from janābah be used for wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about rainwater that runs over a roof on which impurity-related acts occurred. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that when the water flows, there is no harm in using it for wudu for salat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.6 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother, Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)

about a roof where people urinate and perform ritual washing after major impurity (ghusl), and then it rains.
He asked: "Can the water that flows from it be used for ablution (wudu) for prayer?"
Imam (as) said: "If it flows, there is no harm in it."
